EPA's Risk Management Plan
Executive Summary
for Woodbridge Corporations 
SW Foam Plant
El Paso Texas

1. Accidental Release Prevention & Emergency Response Policies

The SW Foam Plant, as part of the Woodbridge-Inoac group of companies, believes the health & safety of its employees and the protection of the natural environment is of the utmost concern in the operation of its business.  We are committed to operating & maintaining all of our processes in a safe & responsible manner.

It is our policy to:

Comply with all applicable laws, regulations, and standards.
Review and assess our operations for the purpose of making health, safety, & environmental improvements.

Our complete Health, Safety, & Environmental policy statement, signed by our plant manager, is posted in the lobby of our facility.

We use a combination of prevention programs and emergency response planning, which are described later in this document, to help ensure the safety of our employees, the public, and to ensure protection of the environment.  Our Plant Manager has the overall responsibility for ensuring that our facility operates in a safe and reliable manner.  This responsibility includes overseeing the implementation of the elements of our risk management program.  To ensure that our risk management program is appropriately developed and implemented, our Plant Manager has assigned the role of RMP Coordinator to the Process Manager who has the background, training, and experience necessary to manage the program.  The RMP Coordinator, acting with the authority delegated directly from the Plant Manager, is responsible for coordinating the development, implementation and integration of the RMP elements as is required under Section 68.15 of the RMP rule.  

2. The Stationary Source & Regulated Substances Handled

The primary purpose of the SW Foam Plant is to produce polyurethane foam for various applications in the automotive industry.  The foam is made using a Varimax machine. It is a contin

uous process slab stock machine that utilizes trough and fall plate technology. The process involves metering the chemicals necessary to produce polyurethane via accurate metering units, these chemicals travel through a system of pipelines from our tank farm to the mixing head where the chemicals are mixed together under controlled conditions and fed into a pre-expansion trough and fall plate system. The fall plate is adapted to the necessary length and configuration so that the foam will reach the horizontal conveyor as a fully expanded slab. The principal expansion takes place downwards over the steeply inclined fall plate which helps us obtain a desired height. The foam travels through the conveyor until it reaches the bun room where it will be moved and placed with the help of an overhead crane and will be left in the bun room to cure for 48hrs before it can be moved to the next process.  


Toluene Diisocyanate (TDI), which is regulated by EPA's risk management program rule, is one of the reactants required to manufacture polyurethane foam.  TDI is received at the plant by railcar and tanker truck and is stored in 2 tanks located in the contained bulk storage tank room.  The TDI is then transferred to the process utilizing a computer-controlled system.

Access to the site is restricted to authorized facility employees, management personnel, and contractors.  The maximum amount of TDI that can be stored at this facility is 300,000 pounds. Our average storage is approximately 250,000 lbs.

3. The General Accidental Release Prevention Program and the Specific Prevention Steps

We take a systematic, proactive approach to preventing accidental releases of chemicals.  Our management systems for our TDI process address each of the key features of successful prevention programs including:

Contractor Awareness
Hot Work Permitting
Monthly Workplace Inspection by members of the Joint Health Safety Committee (JHSC) and management team
Safety Information
Hazard Reviews of

our Processes
Operating Procedures
Training
Equipment Maintenance Programs
RMP Compliance Audits
Accident/Incident Investigation
Standard Operator Training (SOTs)
Annual comprehensive corporate HSE systems auditing

In addition, we have an established Isocyanate Control Program that outlines both the hazards of handling toluene diisocyanate and the controls that are in place to reduce those hazards.  Controls are in place to reduce exposure to employees, the community, and the environment.

These listed individual elements of our prevention program work together to prevent accidental chemical releases.  Our company and our employees are committed to the standard that these management systems are setup for the way we conduct business, and we have specific accountabilities and controls to ensure that we are meeting our own high standards for accident prevention. 

4. Five-year Accident History

The SW Foam Plant has not had any TDI releases that qualify for listing in the EPA's required five-year accident history report.

5. The Emergency Response Plan

We maintain an integrated contingency plan, which consolidates the various federal, state, and local regulatory requirements for emergency response planning.  Our program provides essential planning and training to effectively protect workers, the public, and the environment during emergency situations. We have an internal Emergency Response Team (ERT) that serves as our primary response to any level of spills within our means. In addition, we employ monitoring devices that track the presence of any TDI fumes, which would indicate the release of chemical 5 PPM. As our LEPC and SEPC are one and the same, we have furnished the LEPC with detailed information regarding our primary and alternate release modeling as well as our emergency response procedures. Our Process Manager and HR Manager routinely attend the monthly meetings.  We have also given local hospitals information regarding medical treatment for exposure to TD

I.

6. Planned Changes to Improve Safety

We are constantly looking for more and better ways to improve safety in our processes. Among others, we have installed TDI pumps with magnetic couples, a safer chemical unloading device for non TDI chemical which allow us to unload in a safer way, automatic dispensing system with real time process state via panel views, chemical pipes with improved clamps and fixtures, better dispensing devices (improved pour head, mixer, injectors, etc.), sound alarms, level sensors. The next step under revision is to integrate as much as possible the pouring process to improve safety even more.
